newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks slump on social unease, technicals.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks slump on social unease, technicals.

text.p: Mexican stocks continued their slide towards the close on Thursday on technicals and jitters over the appearance of a manifesto from a new self-styled guerrilla group, traders said.

"Stocks were on offer. The guerrilla business adds to nerves and caution among investors. Foreigners are more interested in the Dow, and now they'll be even less interested in our market," said a trader.
The blue chip IPC index closed down 38.12 points, or 1.14 percent, at 3,320.04 points. Volume was lackluster at 68.8 million shares traded.
A group calling itself the revolutionary Army of Popular Resistance (ERIP) sent a manifesto to several newspapers on Wednesday, which published extracts on Thursday.
The manifesto called for an end of President Zedillo's "repressive" government.
Traders said the manifesto drew attention away from strong third quarter GDP data. The Finance Ministry announced that growth for the quarter was 7.4 percent in real year-on-year terms.
On the broad market, 101 stocks were traded, of which losses outnumbered gains by 59 to 14.
Blue chips were absent from both the leading gains and losers.
A notable loser was market heavyweight Telmex, whose L series shares closed down 14 centavos to 11.96 pesos, while its ADRs ended off 1/8 at 30-1/8.
Technical analysts, meanwhile, pointed out that the Bolsa slumped as it had broken intermediate support at 3,330 points.

"Technically, the market is seeking support at 3,300 points, which is where we shall see whether it is respected and a rally can begin," said Leonor Gonzalez, technical analyst at the BBV-Probursa brokerage.
